In zone UMG, construction footprint (emprise au sol) is not regulated by the zone article 9.

In zone UMG, the quantitative green-space requirements that the public-interest exemption lifts are 20 percent of the site area as green space and 10 percent as open ground (pleine terre) for new construction.
In zone UMG, the maximum height for constructions whose main destination is housing is 20 metres, limited to R+5 levels.
In zone UMG, the maximum height for constructions with any other destination (for example offices) is 18 metres.

In zone UMG, the number of car parking spaces for a public service or collective-interest construction is set case by case from its nature, its grouping, its public-transport access and nearby public car parks, with no fixed ratio (except higher education and research).
In zone UMG, buildings may stand on the alignment of the road or set back by at least 1 metre.
In zone UMG, the setback from a side or rear boundary is at least 6 metres for facades with windows (vues) and at least 3 metres for facades without; building on the boundary is also allowed.
In zone UMG, two buildings on the same plot must be at least 10 metres apart if one of the facing facades has windows (vues), and at least 6 metres if neither has.

facts.key_or_statement: In zone UH of Chevry, the building footprint must not exceed one third (1/3) of the total site area in the zone.
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be set back at least 4 metres from the current or planned alignment.

In zone UH of Chevry, housing requires 2 parking spaces per dwelling in the general case, but 3 spaces per dwelling plus 1 visitor space per 3 dwellings in new housing developments (opérations d'ensemble nouvelles such as lotissements or permis groupés); both cases must be stated.
In zone UH of Chevry, the maximum height to the eaves is 3 metres in sector UHa and 5.50 metres in sector UHb.
In zone UH of Chevry, the maximum number of levels is R+Combles in sector UHa and R+1+Combles in sector UHb.
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be at least 2 metres from the side boundaries (limites séparatives) when there are no windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be at least 4 metres from the side boundaries when there are windows (vues) on the ground floor.
In zone UH of Chevry, windows (vues) on an upper floor may be opened only at least 6 metres from the side boundaries.

In zone UH of Chevry, article 7 on separative boundaries covers the lateral and the rear (fond de terrain) boundaries alike, so the rear setback is the same as the side setback (2 m without windows, 4 m with windows on the ground floor, 6 m for windows on upper floors).
In zone UH of Chevry, several buildings on one property must be at least 8 metres apart if at least one of the two facing facades has windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, several buildings on one property must be at least 4 metres apart if neither facing facade has windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, at least 50 percent of the parking spaces must be covered and integrated in the volume of the building at ground level.
In zone UH of Chevry, one high-stem tree must be planted per 150 m² of land free of construction, with a minimum of 2 trees per site.
In zone UH of Chevry, housing is admitted under the condition that it fits the architectural and landscape harmony of the place.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, the footprint of main constructions (excluding garages and car parks built under a landscaped slab) must not exceed 50 percent of the site area.
coverage.reason: Note 7 (UA9) states that the footprint of main buildings, excluding garages and car parks under a green/pedestrian slab, must not exceed 50% of the plot area, which matches the expected fact. Note 12 only defines emprise au sol and gives no figure.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, the maximum height of a building is 12 metres at the eaves.
coverage.reason: Note 8 (UA10) states "Max 12 m at eaves, 15 m at ridge/top", which matches the expected 12 m maximum building height at the eaves in UA. No other note gives this rule with this figure.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, the maximum height is 15 metres at the ridge (faîtage, faîte or ceiling height).
coverage.reason: Note [8] states the UA10 height rule: "Max 12 m at eaves, 15 m at ridge/top", which matches the expected 15 m at the ridge for zone UA of Chevry. No other note gives this figure.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, the number of levels is limited to R+3, including converted attics.
coverage.reason: Note 8 (UA10) states the limit as "R+3 levels (including habitable attic)", which is the same rule, scope and condition as the expected fact; no other note gives a level limit.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, constructions may be set either at the alignment or set back from it; there is no minimum road setback and no obligation to build on the alignment.
coverage.reason: Note 3 says under UA6 that "buildings may be built at the alignment or set back", with no minimum setback or obligation to build on the alignment. It gives the same rule for the same zone, and its 3 m condition only governs where a wall or garage may stand at the alignment. Other notes either cover side or rear boundaries or are on other topics.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, constructions may be built on a lateral boundary or set back from it.
coverage.reason: Note 4 states that under UA7 'Buildings may be on the lateral boundary or set back', which is the expected fact. Note 5 repeats the explicit option to build on the lateral boundary, but it is mainly about the rear boundary and only says the same eaves-height setback applies otherwise; it adds no separate rule beyond Note 4, so I do not count it.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, a construction set back from the side boundary must be at a distance at least equal to its height measured at the eaves (at the highest point of the ground), with no distinction between facades with and without views.
coverage.reason: Note 4 states UA7: if set back from the lateral boundary, distance at least equal to the building height at the eaves, measured at the highest point of the ground, with no views distinction. Note 5 repeats the same eaves-height rule but concerns the rear boundary, so it does not state the side rule on its own; note 6 gives a different rule with 4 m/8 m minimums.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, two buildings on the same property must be separated by at least the height at the eaves of the taller building, and not less than 4 metres where the facing facades have no views or 8 metres otherwise.
coverage.reason: Note 6 (UA8) gives the same rule: distance between buildings on the same property at least the taller building's eaves height, and not less than 4 m where facades have no views, 8 m otherwise.

coverage.statement: Housing in zone UA of Chevry requires 2 parking spaces per dwelling.
coverage.reason: Note 10 states "UA12: housing requires 2 places per dwelling", which matches the expected rule on figure, scope (housing, zone UA) and condition. No other note gives a parking ratio.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, at least 50 percent of the parking spaces attached to dwellings must be built in the basement or on the ground floor of the buildings.
coverage.reason: Note [10] (UA12) says "at least 50% of the places attached to dwellings must be built in basement or ground floor of buildings", which is the same rule with the same figure, scope and condition.

coverage.statement: In zone UA of Chevry, the facades of residential buildings may not exceed 25 metres in a single vertical plane.
coverage.reason: Note 9 states "Residential façades may not exceed 25 m in a single vertical plane" under UA11, which matches the expected rule with the same figure, scope and zone.

facts.key_or_statement: In sector UM4, the maximum height of constructions whose main destination is housing is 20 metres.

Housing parking in zone UM requires 1 space per 35 m² of floor area (surface de plancher), capped at 2 spaces per dwelling.
Dwellings financed with a State-aided loan require 1 parking space per dwelling in zone UM.
Student residences in zone UM require 1 parking space per 150 m² of floor area.
Housing in zone UM requires bicycle parking only for buildings of more than three dwellings, at 0.75 m² per dwelling up to two main rooms and 1.5 m² per dwelling otherwise.
For housing in zone UM, at least 85 percent of the motorised parking spaces built on the plot must be integrated into the housing building, a majority of them underground.
Zone UM setback from the road alignment (voies et emprises publiques) - a construction may be built on the alignment or set back, and a setback must be at least 1 metre.
Zone UM side and rear boundaries - constructions may be built on one or several boundaries, or set back from them.
Zone UM boundary setback for facades with windows (vues) up to 12 metres high is half the facade height, with a minimum of 5 metres.
Zone UM boundary setback for facades with windows (vues) higher than 12 metres is 6 metres.
Zone UM boundary setback for facades without windows (vues) is at least 3 metres.
Zone UM distance between buildings on the same plot is 10 metres if at least one of the facing facades has windows (vues), 3 metres if neither does, unless the buildings are attached.
Zone UM green space - new construction must treat at least 20 percent of the plot area as green space (espace vert) and at least 10 percent as deep soil (pleine terre).

Zone UM maximum height is measured from the natural ground before works to the top of the ridge or acroterion, technical structures included except small ones (under 20 percent of the footprint and under 2 metres high).
Every project in zone UM must be compatible with the orientations of the OAP (pièce n°3 of the PLU).

facts.key_or_statement: In sector UM5a, the maximum height of buildings whose main destination is housing is 20 metres, the same limit as for housing in UM5.
In sector UM5a, housing buildings are also limited to R+5 (a maximum of six levels above ground).

reads.fact: In sector UGc, the construction footprint of buildings must not exceed 30 percent of the total site area in the zone (the general UG rule, which excludes only UGa, UGb and UGd).
In sector UGc, the footprint of ancillary constructions must not exceed 8 percent of the site area.
In sector UGc, the height of a main building must not exceed 7 metres at the eaves or at the acroterion (the general UG rule, which excludes UGa, UGd, UGf and UGg).
In sector UGc, the height of a main building must not exceed 10 metres at the ridge (faîtage, faîte) or at the ceiling height (hauteur plafond).
In sector UGc, the height of ancillary constructions must not exceed 2.50 metres at the eaves and 3 metres at the acroterion.
In sector UGc, buildings must be set back from the road alignment (the sector rule says they are built "en retrait"), so building on the alignment is not permitted there.
In UGc, a main building facade, or part of a facade, with views (vues) must stand at least 8 metres from the side boundary.
In UGc, a facade without views must stand from the side boundary at a distance of at least half the building height measured at the eaves (L=1/2H), with a minimum of 2 metres.
The rear boundary (limite de fond de terrain) is treated as a separative boundary under UG article 7, so the same setback rules apply to the rear as to the sides.
In UGc, two buildings on the same property must be at least half the height of the taller building (measured at the eaves) apart, with a minimum of 4 metres, when the facing facades have no views.
In UGc, two buildings on the same property must be at least the height of the taller building (measured at the eaves) apart, with a minimum of 8 metres, when one of the facing facades has views.
In UGc, two buildings on the same property must be at least 1.5 times the height of the taller building (measured at the eaves) apart, with a minimum of 16 metres, when the facing facades have views.

In UGc, at least 50 percent of the required parking spaces must be covered or built underground (the rule excludes only UGa and UGb), except visitor spaces and spaces for collective facilities, and does not apply in flood zones.
For housing of more than three dwellings, bicycle parking requires 0.75 m² per dwelling for dwellings up to two main rooms and 1.5 m² per dwelling otherwise.
Sector UGc of the Vallée zone UG corresponds to the site near the Courcelle station.

facts.key_or_statement: In UHe, the footprint of main buildings must not exceed 20 percent of the site area (article UH9 rule "En UH et UHe et UHf").
In UHe, the footprint of ancillary buildings must not exceed 5 percent of the site area, and terraces and swimming pools count as footprint.
UHe has no height rule of its own; the general UH rule (UH outside UHf) applies, so a main building is limited to 7 metres at the eaves or the acroterion.
Under the same UH rule, a main building is limited to 10 metres at the ridge (faîtage, faîte or ceiling height).
Under the same UH rule, the number of levels of a main building is limited to R+1+combles.

Parking for housing in UHe is 2 spaces per dwelling, one of them covered, as the general rule; but in new housing operations of more than 3 dwellings (subdivision, grouped permits, collective buildings) 3 spaces per dwelling and 1 visitor space per 3 dwellings are required instead (all zones except UHc).

Beyond the 25 metre strip measured from the serving roads, only terraces and ancillary buildings (garages, garden sheds, uncovered pools and their technical works) are allowed, so a new dwelling must sit within the strip.

Setback from roads in UH outside UHf is 9 metres from the road axis when the road right-of-way is under 8 metres, and 5 metres from the alignment when the right-of-way is 8 metres or more or for public spaces.
Setback from side and rear boundaries must be at least 8 metres where the facade has views, and half the facade height (H/2) with a minimum of 2 metres where it has none.
Several buildings on one plot must be at least 8 metres apart if at least one of the facing facades has views, and 4 metres apart if neither has views.
In UH, UHe and UHf, vegetated spaces must cover at least 70 percent of the site area.

What sets UHe apart is the residual radioactive contamination of its districts (Coudraies, Clos Rose); the regulation only allows dwellings or extensions of existing buildings there, under conditions.
In UHe, any exploitation of subsoil natural resources (quarry, water abstraction, hydrocarbons) is additionally forbidden.

In the prescription perimeter, housing construction and works, with their outbuildings and garages, are authorised provided that any work requiring excavation is accompanied by removal of the soil by an approved body to a specialised treatment or storage centre.

In the prescription perimeter, excavation deeper than 50 cm over a surface of 10 m² or more requires prior information of the municipal services and a prior radiological mapping (dose rate) of the area.
In the prescription perimeter, a check of the bottom of the excavation must be done before the foundations are laid.

facts.key_or_statement: In zone N (Vallée), article N1 prohibits, throughout the zone and its sectors, new constructions, works or structures for housing (habitation), other than those admitted by article N2.

In zone N (Vallée), article N2 does not admit any new dwelling in the plain zone; the only housing-related use it admits for the whole zone is the extension of dwellings existing at the approval date of the PLU, limited to 15 percent of their floor area (surface de plancher).
In zone N (Vallée), new housing is therefore not permitted, so no buildable envelope for new dwellings exists in the plain zone N.
The 20 percent extension limit for existing constructions applies only in the sector Nc, not in the plain zone N.
Housing-related development linked to existing activities (aménagement d’habitat) is admitted only in the sector Nca, and only for activities authorised in existing buildings.
The footprint limit of 15 percent in article N9 applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL; for the other sectors, including plain zone N, it is "sans objet".
Under article N10, the height of constructions in plain zone N is not regulated; the 10 metre ridge limit applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL.
Under article N6, constructions must be set back at least 12 metres from the axis of the road or from the limits of public land (emprise publique).
Under article N7, the setback from property boundaries (limites séparatives) must be at least 16 metres, and 8 metres only in Nca.
Under article N8, the distance between several buildings on one property is not regulated in zone N and the sector NL; the 8 metre minimum applies only in the sectors Nc and Nca.
The regulation's Titre III lists an emplacement réservé Z at the Impasse de la Gourdillerie, a turning area (aire de retournement) of 490 m² for the commune.
Under Titre III, construction is prohibited on land, built or not, included in an emplacement réservé, subject to the Code de l’urbanisme.

statements.key_or_statement: In zone N (Vallée), article N1 prohibits, throughout the zone and its sectors, new constructions, works or structures for housing (habitation), other than those admitted by article N2.

In zone N (Vallée), article N2 does not admit any new dwelling in the plain zone; the only housing-related use it admits for the whole zone is the extension of dwellings existing at the approval date of the PLU, limited to 15 percent of their floor area (surface de plancher).
In zone N (Vallée), new housing is therefore not permitted, so no buildable envelope for new dwellings exists in the plain zone N.
The 20 percent extension limit for existing constructions applies only in the sector Nc, not in the plain zone N.
Housing-related development linked to existing activities (aménagement d’habitat) is admitted only in the sector Nca, and only for activities authorised in existing buildings.
The footprint limit of 15 percent in article N9 applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL; for the other sectors, including plain zone N, it is "sans objet".
Under article N10, the height of constructions in plain zone N is not regulated; the 10 metre ridge limit applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL.
Under article N6, constructions must be set back at least 12 metres from the axis of the road or from the limits of public land (emprise publique).
Under article N7, the setback from property boundaries (limites séparatives) must be at least 16 metres, and 8 metres only in Nca.
Under article N8, the distance between several buildings on one property is not regulated in zone N and the sector NL; the 8 metre minimum applies only in the sectors Nc and Nca.
The regulation's Titre III lists an emplacement réservé Z at the Impasse de la Gourdillerie, a turning area (aire de retournement) of 490 m² for the commune.
Under Titre III, construction is prohibited on land, built or not, included in an emplacement réservé, subject to the Code de l’urbanisme.
